jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Data Products
jobs.description:
At Counterpart Health, we are transforming healthcare and improving patient care with our innovative primary care tool, Counterpart Assistant. By supporting Primary Care Physicians (PCPs), we are able to deliver improved outcomes to our patients at a lower cost through early diagnosis and longitudinal care management of chronic conditions.

We're looking for a Director of Engineering to lead our Data Products pillar, serving as the technical engine for Counterpart Health's (CPH) clinical-data foundation. You will own the technical strategy and execution for the Data Products roadmap—encompassing clinical data ingestion, canonical data modeling, and ingestion scalability—while building scalable, reusable data capabilities that serve as a foundational platform for driving clinical insight generation. You will own the technical strategy for our Data Products platform—ensuring our clinical data foundations (using standards like FHIR, LOINC, and RxNorm) effectively drive business outcomes. You will serve as a critical leader and partner to the VP of Engineering and cross-functional leaders in Product, Data Science, and Design.

As a Director Of Engineering, Data Products, You Will

Own the Data Products technical roadmap, canonical data modeling, and ingestion scalability.
Manage and optimize the clinical data ingestion pipeline.
Oversee the scaling of customer data onboarding processes and the continuous improvement of data hygiene, canonical storage standards, and observability and monitoring of the data pipelines.
Enable shared funnel visibility across the organization and support the development of a robust enterprise reporting framework.
Drive the adoption of an AI-powered Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), leveraging AI tools to accelerate coding, testing, and deployment processes while maintaining stringent code quality and security standards.

Success In This Role Looks Like

Successfully achieving improved clinical data coverage and freshness targets across all patient populations.
Predictable and repeatable multi-customer scaling with standardized playbooks for rapid data readiness.
Broad adoption of the Data Products platform and its capabilities
Data infrastructure is robust, stable, and serves as a reliable source of truth during rapid organizational growth and customer expansion.

You Should Get In Touch If

You possess 10+ years of engineering experience with a deep focus on building high-scale data platforms, distributed systems, and interoperability standards (e.g., FHIR, CCDA).
Proven track record in managing and scaling engineering teams that handle data-heavy workloads and complex clinical data pipelines.
Proven experience leading cross-functional teams of engineers to deliver complex software in regulated environments.
Experience implementing and scaling AI-assisted development workflows (e.g., AI code assistants, automated testing, or AI-driven SDLC) to improve engineering productivity.
Demonstrated experience building and managing engineering systems in highly regulated healthcare environments, with a strong operational understanding of HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance requirements.
Passionate about the healthcare sector and committed to utilizing technical expertise to drive meaningful improvements in patient outcomes.
Deeply familiar with the inherent complexities and lack of standardization in clinical datasets, with a proactive focus on enhancing data integrity.
Motivated by intricate technical challenges and dedicated to architecting pragmatic, high-quality engineering solutions through continuous intellectual exploration.
Thrives in dynamic, high-growth environments, demonstrating the ability to navigate ambiguity and align technical priorities with overarching strategic objectives.
Action-oriented leader who assumes full ownership of system sustainability, willing to address operational gaps to ensure the team achieves its delivery milestones.

Engineering Leadership Skills

Proven track record of directly hiring, mentoring, and developing engineering managers, Tech Leads (TLs), and Principal Engineers (PELs).
Demonstrated ability to cultivate a high-performance engineering culture focused on velocity, quality, and psychological safety.
Experience leading organizational change, including structural re-orgs and process evolution.
Strong proficiency in strategic resource allocation, capacity planning, and managing technical debt in a fast-paced product environment.
Exceptional stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical constraints into clear, actionable business strategies (e.g., impact on HEDIS/RADV outcomes) for non-technical leadership.

Benefits Overview

Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive group medical coverage that include coverage for hospitalization, outpatient care, optical services, and dental benefits.
Mental Well-Being: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous annual leave policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.
Professional Development: We are committed to developing our talent professionally. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks

Reimbursement for office setup expenses
Monthly cell phone & internet stipend
Flexibility to work from home, enabling collaboration with global teams
Paid parental leave for all new parents
And much more!

About Counterpart Health:
In 2018, Clover Health set out to do something unprecedented: build a clinically intuitive, AI-enabled solution that fits within physicians' workflows to help support the earlier diagnosis and management of chronic conditions.

Years later, that vision is a reality, with thousands of practitioners using Counterpart Assistant during patient visits to improve disease management, reduce medical expenses, and drive success in value-based care.

With an exceptional team of value-based care and technology experts, Counterpart Health is driving value-based care at the speed of software.

Counterpart Health is a subsidiary of Clover Health. From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We are an E-Verify company.

Final pay is based on several factors including but not limited to internal equity, market data, and the applicant’s education, work experience, certifications, etc.

A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is:

$223,100—$290,000 USD

jobs.title: Director, Mission Engineering Department
jobs.description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Enterprise Effects Division (EED) drives integration of Aerospace’s strategic capabilities across the national space enterprise. The division leverages a broad array of engineering disciplines against dynamic portfolio of programs, customers, and national challenges. EED spans the capability lifecycle from concept and architecture design to performance assessment to application of space and space-enabled capabilities.

As part of the Enterprise Design Subdivision (EDS), the Mission Engineering Department provides technical expertise and leadership in mission engineering methods, processes, and tools to a wide range of customers, including National Security Space (NSS), defense programs, NASA, NOAA, NNSA, and others. The department evaluates customer mission-integration needs, develops end-to-end mission threads, and offers recommendations to enterprise leaders on risks, issues, and gaps, ultimately developing solutions to achieve desired mission outcomes. The Director of the Mission Engineering Department will lead these efforts, build partnerships with customers, and ensure the team is staffed with top talent to solve complex challenges.

Work Model:

This full-time position requires 100% onsite work in El Segundo CA, Chantilly, VA, or Colorado Springs, CO.

What You’ll Be Doing:  

Develop and execute the vision for the department, enhancing corporate capabilities to support customer architecture, systems-of-systems, and enterprise decisions.
Scale the department’s capabilities through recruiting, onboarding, and developing staff via performance management, mentoring, and coaching.
Ensure the Mission Engineering Department and related corporate activities fully leverage expertise from across Aerospace, incorporating best practices in enterprise systems engineering.
Manage the department, including staff performance reviews, resource allocation, and personnel management, and recommend performance improvements, career development, personnel actions, and awards.
Serve as the primary contact for program office inquiries, using mission engineering principles to define problem spaces, develop implementation plans, and identify appropriate personnel based on expertise.
Foster a culture of innovation and collaboration, maintain robust relationships with peer organizations, and lead multi-discipline analyst teams.
Identify new partnerships for future mission engineering growth in customer impact.
Coordinate and manage complex technical tasks among customers, ensuring quality and accuracy of work products.
Collaborate with subdivision leadership to cultivate an effective national organization.
Lead technical activities, organize project teams, and execute a variety of architecture conceptualization, assessment, analysis, and mission engineering activities.

What You Need to be a Successful Director, Mission Engineering Department

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, physics, operations research, mathematics, or a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution and equivalent technical experience
Typically 10 or more years demonstrated experience leading engineering studies and analysis teams, managing/coordinating complex technical tasks among team members, and translating customer needs into actionable tasks for analysts
Demonstrated leadership of multidisciplinary teams involving system design, acquisition and/or operations in one or more of the following areas: space systems, ground systems, launch systems, or operations
Experience in hiring, supervising, developing, mentoring, and inspiring staff
Proven ability to initiate and lead project teams, develop project plans, identify high-impact deliverables, and manage schedule commitments
Exceptional time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and to lead cross-functional teams
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to present methods and results effectively
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, adapt quickly to change, manage ambiguity, and demonstrate initiative under pressure
Ability to travel approximately 15-25% of the time
This position requires a current and active TS/SCI clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government, and the ability to pass a CI Polygraph. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance.

How You Can Stand Out  

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these: 

A graduate degree or extensive work experience relevant fields
Experience with model-based systems engineering (MBSE) and/or digital engineering
Experience collaborating with multiple Aerospace program offices and customers
Strong interpersonal networks within Aerospace and customer organizations
Military operations experience in the space, air, land, or sea domains
Experience with Intelligence Community systems engineering and programmatic processes
Experience with spacecraft, payloads, ground systems, launch systems, missile systems, nuclear weapon systems, and/or aircraft systems
A proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with contractors, customers, and corporate staff

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. The grade-based pay range for this job is listed below. Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills.

(Min - Max)

$168,200.00 - $252,400.00

Pay Basis: Annual

Leadership Competencies

Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who:

Operate Strategically
Lead Change  
Engage with Impact  
Foster Innovation  
Deliver Results

Ways We Reward Our Employees

During your interview process, our team will provide details of our industry-leading benefits.

Benefits vary and are applicable based on Job Type. A few highlights include:

Comprehensive health care and wellness plans
Paid holidays, sick time, and vacation
Standard and alternate work schedules, including telework options
401(k) Plan — Employees receive a total company-paid benefit of 8%, 10%, or 12% of eligible compensation based on years of service and matching contributions; employees are immediately eligible and vested in the plan upon hire
Flexible spending accounts
Variable pay program for exceptional contributions
Relocation assistance
Professional growth and development programs to help advance your career
Education assistance programs
An inclusive work environment built on teamwork, flexibility, and respect

We are all unique, from various backgrounds and all walks of life, yet one thing bonds all of us to each other—the belief that we can make a difference. This core belief empowers us to do our best work at The Aerospace Corporation.

Equal Opportunity Commitment

The Aerospace Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, color, religion, genetic information, marital status, ancestry, national origin, protected veteran status, physical disability, medical condition, mental disability, or disability status and any other characteristic protected by state or federal law. If you’re an individual with a disability or a disabled veteran who needs assistance using our online job search and application tools or need reasonable accommodation to complete the job application process, please contact us by phone at 310.336.5432 or by email at peoplemangmnt.mailbox@aero.org . You can also review Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal.

jobs.title: Technical Director, Traffic Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is seeking an experienced and highly motivated Technical Director, Traffic Engineering
to join our team in New York. This role can be based in any of the following NY offices: Valhalla, NYC, Buffalo, or Troy
.

The ideal candidate is an experienced Traffic Engineer who is innovative, results-oriented, and team-focused. The right candidate would be joining a tight-knit team of traffic engineers and transportation planners who value technical excellence, career development, pride in our work, a collaborative team environment, and a passion for finding the right solutions that enhance mobility and safety. The Technical Director, Traffic Engineering will bring and leadership skills to help grow our business, oversee project delivery and staff development, and provide technical assistance and guidance in engineering and design for our local, state, and regional clients. Our ideal candidate has a proven track record of successfully delivering projects from initiation through operations and maintenance, with a strong focus on client satisfaction and technical excellence. This position will primarily support projects in New York. .Some project-related travel may be required.

Your Impact

Support the delivery and execution of project scope, objectives, and requirements, ensuring close collaboration and alignment with clients and stakeholders. Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate project risks and issues. Ensure project deliverables meet high-quality standards and specified requirements. Implement rigorous quality review processes, manage version controls, and track comments and resolutions. Prepare and present comprehensive project progress statuses using reporting tools and dashboards. Monitor and meet defined performance metrics, tracking budget, time, scope, and communication details to ensure projects meet schedule and client expectations.
Stay current with emerging technologies, industry best practices, and relevant standards .
Lead and direct multi-disciplinary project teams, including internal staff, sub-consultants, contractors, and vendors. Foster a culture of trust, transparency, and accountability.
Manage internal groups or outside vendors to identify, plan, negotiating contracts, deliver and monitoring performance to client specifications.
Coordinate with various internal and external partners, including cross-discipline and functional teams, government agencies (i.e., DOTs), and other stakeholders.
Comfortably present complex technical and project information to diverse audiences, including executives, client teams, and public forums.
Contribute to and potentially lead the development of technical proposals, scopes of work, and budgeting for projected work.
Assist in building and growing the firm's Traffic Engineering, Safety and Intelligent Transportation Systems practice across New York State.
Foster technical development and mentoring of staff.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Traffic Engineering, Computer Science, or Information Technology, preferred, or equivalent years of experience.
12+ years of progressive experience in traffic, ITS, & safety planning, analysis, and design.
Licensed Professional Engineer in the State of New York, or another state and able to obtain reciprocity in New York State within 6 months of hire. PTOE certification (highly preferred).
Proven experience managing complex projects with budgets, schedules, and technical requirements.
Proven experience with NYSDOT, MTA, and other regional agencies.
Develop new project opportunities, manage client relationships, and prepare and manage proposal submissions
Strong leadership, mentoring, and team-building skills.
Exceptional communication abilities including written, verbal, and public speaking.
Demonstrated success in proposal writing, client presentations, and strategic project delivery.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment.
Passion for innovation, quality, and financial performance
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Strong ability to quickly adapt to change and demonstrate flexibility to a variety of schedules and hours to meet business needs.
Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Engineering.
Active engagement in relevant industry organizations.
Project experience - Traffic operations and safety, ATSPM, signal design, signal timing, NYSDOT experience, Interstate Reconstruction, Environmental Impact Statements.
Expertise in traffic engineering principles, practices, NYSDOT project delivery process, Traffic Signal Design, Signage, pavement markings, Maco, Meso and Micro-simulation modeling.

WSP Benefits:

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on a providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation:

Expected Salary (all locations): $139,800 - $249,150

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and may offer additional benefits and compensation, depending on circumstances and the type of work being performed not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

www.wsp.com

WSP provides a flexible and agile workplace model while meeting client needs. Employees are also afforded a comprehensive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, life, and retirement savings focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career.

At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

WSP USA (and all of its U.S. companies) is an Equal Opportunity Employer Race/Age/Color/Religion/Sex/Sexual Orientation/Gender Identity/National Origin/Disability or Protected Veteran Status.

The selected candidate must be authorized to work in the United States.

NOTICE TO THIRD PARTY AGENCIES:

WSP does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters, employment agencies, or other staffing services. Unsolicited resumes include any resume or hiring document sent to WSP in the absence of a signed Service Agreement where WSP has expressly requested recruitment/staffing services specific to the position at hand. Any unsolicited resumes, including those submitted to hiring managers or other business leaders, will become the property of WSP and WSP will have the right to hire that candidate without reservation – no fee or other compensation will be owed or paid to the recruiter, employment agency, or other staffing service.

If you already have a profile with us, you can log in to check status.

Need Help?

Regular or Temporary:

Regular

Language Fluency:

1st shift (United States of America)

Please review the following job description:

The Senior Director, Agentic Engineering serves as the executive leader of Forge's agentic engineering organization and is accountable for the technical vision, engineering execution, and operational excellence behind Truist's enterprise AI agent ecosystem. This leader owns the engineering function responsible for designing, building, deploying, and operating production-grade AI agents, multi-agent systems, and agentic workflows that transform how teammates and clients interact with the Firm.

This is a highly technical player-coach leadership role that combines executive organizational leadership with deep hands-on engineering expertise. The Senior Director leads the engineering function, establishes technical direction, drives work planning and execution, and serves as the ultimate escalation point for architecture and engineering decisions across the agentic engineering portfolio.

The successful candidate will bring extensive experience building large-scale software and AI systems, including expertise in Python, modern systems languages such as Go, agentic frameworks, LLM orchestration, retrieval architectures, and enterprise AI platform engineering. This leader will be responsible for shipping production agentic systems, not simply defining roadmaps, ensuring all solutions meet Truist standards for security, scalability, resiliency, observability, governance, and regulatory compliance.

The Senior Director partners closely with Product, Architecture, Security, Platform Engineering, Data Engineering, Risk, and executive leadership teams to translate business strategy into enterprise-scale AI capabilities while building and mentoring a world-class team of agentic engineers.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Following is a summary of the essential functions for this job. Other duties may be performed, both major and minor, which are not mentioned below. Specific activities may change from time to time.

Lead the Agentic Engineering function, providing executive leadership, organizational design, technical governance, delivery accountability, and talent leadership across all agentic engineering initiatives.
Own the technical direction for Forge agentic solutions, establishing architecture standards, engineering patterns, and development practices for enterprise AI agents and multi-agent systems.
Drive work planning, prioritization, execution management, and delivery outcomes across the agentic engineering organization, ensuring teams consistently deliver high-quality production systems aligned to business commitments.
Serve as the final engineering authority for architecture decisions, engineering standards, and critical code review escalations across the agentic engineering portfolio.
Design and govern enterprise patterns for agent orchestration, tool invocation, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), memory management, prompt architecture, workflow automation, reasoning frameworks, evaluation pipelines, observability, and operational support.
Lead the engineering strategy for enterprise agent platforms including Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, and other emerging agentic technologies required to support the Forge roadmap.
Partner with Product, Technology, Security, Risk, Architecture, and Data leaders to ensure AI solutions are secure, compliant, scalable, and aligned to enterprise priorities.
Build and mentor a high-performing engineering organization through hiring, performance management, succession planning, coaching, career development, and technical leadership.
Establish and enforce engineering excellence standards including software craftsmanship, testing strategies, release management, architecture review, secure development practices, operational readiness, and reliability engineering.
Drive engineering execution across complex cross-functional initiatives involving application engineering, platform engineering, data engineering, AI engineering, cyber security, and enterprise architecture teams.
Champion engineering rigor through measurable quality controls, system reliability objectives, operational metrics, and continuous improvement practices.
Evaluate emerging AI technologies, frameworks, models, and engineering approaches, identifying opportunities to accelerate delivery, improve reliability, and strengthen enterprise capabilities
Represent Agentic Engineering in executive governance forums, architecture review boards, risk committees, vendor engagements, regulatory discussions, and industry working groups.
Manage organizational budgets, vendor relationships, workforce planning, engineering tooling investments, and resource allocation to support strategic objectives.
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, engineering excellence, continuous learning, and responsible AI development across the organization

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, a related field, or equivalent education, training and work-related experience.
Minimum of 12 years of progressive experience in technology operations.
Broad leadership and management experience leading complex technology operations teams.
Proven ability to manage complex operational initiatives across multiple teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading enterprise Agentic Engineering, AI Platform Engineering, Applied AI, Intelligent Automation, or Emerging Technology organizations.
Deep expertise in multi-agent systems, agent orchestration frameworks, prompt engineering, reasoning architectures, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), memory systems, agent evaluation, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
Experience building production AI applications using Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Semantic Kernel, LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Google Vertex AI Agent Engine, or similar platforms.
Experience operating enterprise-scale AI platforms supporting thousands of users and mission-critical business processes.
Strong understanding of AI governance, model risk management, responsible AI principles, AI security controls, and enterprise AI operating models.
Demonstrated ability to establish engineering standards, mentor senior engineers and engineering leaders, and build a culture of technical excellence.
Experience delivering solutions across cloud-native ecosystems using Azure and modern DevOps, platform engineering, and software delivery practices.

Technology Operations owns independently determining whether it meets the agreed requirements.

A project is not complete because code exists.
It is complete when it meets its acceptance criteria and works in production.

Documentation & Key-Person Risk

Make sure critical company technology does not exist only inside someone's head.
Establish documentation requirements covering:
System architecture
Infrastructure
Databases
Data flows
APIs
AI agents
Repositories
Deployment procedures
Environments
Integrations
Vendors
Access requirements
Technical decisions
Runbooks
Recovery procedures

Engineering creates and maintains technical documentation.

You verify that required documentation exists, is current and can actually be used by another qualified person.

Security Governance & Operational Resilience

Establish visibility and accountability around:
Infrastructure access
Credentials and permissions
Source-code repositories
Production environments
Data security
Vendors
Backup and recovery
Business continuity
Incident response
Security policies
Technical risk

You are not expected to personally operate every security system.
You ensure appropriate controls exist, ownership is clear and material risks are surfaced.

Technology Risk

Maintain a technology risk register covering areas such as:
Key-person dependency
Security exposure
Infrastructure concentration
Undocumented systems
Vendor dependency
Data risks
Production instability
Recovery capability
Technical operational risk

Escalate material risks directly to leadership.

CEO Technology Visibility

Create a simple executive technology dashboard that answers:
What are we building?

Who owns it?

When was it promised?

What's at risk?

What's blocked?

What shipped?

Did it pass QA?

Does it work in production?

Is it documented?

The CEO should not have to chase engineers for answers.

What You Do NOT Own

You do not
own:
Writing production software
Engineering architecture
Engineering implementation
Managing software engineers
Assigning engineering resources
Code reviews
Choosing frameworks
Building AI agents
Technical product development
Resolving engineering problems yourself

Those responsibilities belong to the Director of Engineering and Chief Architect/CTO.

Your role is to measure, verify, challenge, document and escalate—not become a shadow engineering department.

First 90 Days

First 30 Days:
Map projects, commitments, systems, ownership, access, documentation, security exposure and key-person risks. Establish the technology source of truth.

By Day 60:
Implement delivery reporting, QA standards, acceptance criteria, documentation requirements, risk tracking and CEO reporting.

By Day 90:
Establish a repeatable Technology Assurance operating system providing independent visibility into whether engineering is delivering working, documented and resilient technology.

How Success Is Measured

Can leadership see exactly what engineering is working on?
Are commitments and dates explicit?
Are missed commitments identified early?
Does released technology pass independent verification?
Are defects being identified systematically?
Is critical technology documented?
Is key-person dependency decreasing?
Are security risks visible?
Are operational risks being addressed?
Can leadership understand technology status without chasing engineers?

Your job is to create accountability and assurance without creating bureaucracy.

You will set direction, strengthen leadership capacity, remove barriers, and use data and responsible AI to improve attendee experience and operating efficiency.

The impact you will have

Sustain and strengthen a high-performing event technology organization with clear structure, career paths, leadership capacity, and staffing plans aligned to a growing global event portfolio; success is measured through team retention, development progress, leadership depth, and delivery capacity.
Own and advance a prioritized, multi-year event technology roadmap aligned with marketing leadership across Data + AI Summit, Data + AI World Tour, AI Days, executive programs, and field events; success is measured through roadmap delivery, stakeholder alignment, and adoption of agreed capabilities.
Keep a complex event technology ecosystem launch-ready, reliable, and scalable across registration, event management, mobile apps, meetings, content, check-in and badging, signage, streaming, onsite AV, production, network, and IT; success is measured through service performance, readiness milestones, and fewer critical event technology issues.

Strengthen and steward a trusted event data foundation that connects registration, attendance, and engagement data with Salesforce, Marketo, the Databricks platform, and reporting partners; success is measured through reconciled data, accurate reporting, and reliable access for Analytics, Marketing, and Sales Operations.

Reinforce consistent ways of working across programs—including requirements, intake, prioritization, testing, UAT, documentation, and retrospectives—so teams deliver repeatable, predictable event experiences; success is measured through adoption of operating standards and improved execution consistency.

jobs.title: Director, Mission Engineering Department
jobs.description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Enterprise Effects Division (EED) drives integration of Aerospace’s strategic capabilities across the national space enterprise. The division leverages a broad array of engineering disciplines against dynamic portfolio of programs, customers, and national challenges. EED spans the capability lifecycle from concept and architecture design to performance assessment to application of space and space-enabled capabilities.

As part of the Enterprise Design Subdivision (EDS), the Mission Engineering Department provides technical expertise and leadership in mission engineering methods, processes, and tools to a wide range of customers, including National Security Space (NSS), defense programs, NASA, NOAA, NNSA, and others. The department evaluates customer mission-integration needs, develops end-to-end mission threads, and offers recommendations to enterprise leaders on risks, issues, and gaps, ultimately developing solutions to achieve desired mission outcomes. The Director of the Mission Engineering Department will lead these efforts, build partnerships with customers, and ensure the team is staffed with top talent to solve complex challenges.

Work Model:

This full-time position requires 100% onsite work in El Segundo CA, Chantilly, VA, or Colorado Springs, CO.

What You’ll Be Doing:  

Develop and execute the vision for the department, enhancing corporate capabilities to support customer architecture, systems-of-systems, and enterprise decisions.
Scale the department’s capabilities through recruiting, onboarding, and developing staff via performance management, mentoring, and coaching.
Ensure the Mission Engineering Department and related corporate activities fully leverage expertise from across Aerospace, incorporating best practices in enterprise systems engineering.
Manage the department, including staff performance reviews, resource allocation, and personnel management, and recommend performance improvements, career development, personnel actions, and awards.
Serve as the primary contact for program office inquiries, using mission engineering principles to define problem spaces, develop implementation plans, and identify appropriate personnel based on expertise.
Foster a culture of innovation and collaboration, maintain robust relationships with peer organizations, and lead multi-discipline analyst teams.
Identify new partnerships for future mission engineering growth in customer impact.
Coordinate and manage complex technical tasks among customers, ensuring quality and accuracy of work products.
Collaborate with subdivision leadership to cultivate an effective national organization.
Lead technical activities, organize project teams, and execute a variety of architecture conceptualization, assessment, analysis, and mission engineering activities.

What You Need to be a Successful Director, Mission Engineering Department

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, physics, operations research, mathematics, or a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution and equivalent technical experience
Typically 10 or more years demonstrated experience leading engineering studies and analysis teams, managing/coordinating complex technical tasks among team members, and translating customer needs into actionable tasks for analysts
Demonstrated leadership of multidisciplinary teams involving system design, acquisition and/or operations in one or more of the following areas: space systems, ground systems, launch systems, or operations
Experience in hiring, supervising, developing, mentoring, and inspiring staff
Proven ability to initiate and lead project teams, develop project plans, identify high-impact deliverables, and manage schedule commitments
Exceptional time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and to lead cross-functional teams
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to present methods and results effectively
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, adapt quickly to change, manage ambiguity, and demonstrate initiative under pressure
Ability to travel approximately 15-25% of the time
This position requires a current and active TS/SCI clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government, and the ability to pass a CI Polygraph. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance.

How You Can Stand Out  

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these: 

A graduate degree or extensive work experience relevant fields
Experience with model-based systems engineering (MBSE) and/or digital engineering
Experience collaborating with multiple Aerospace program offices and customers
Strong interpersonal networks within Aerospace and customer organizations
Military operations experience in the space, air, land, or sea domains
Experience with Intelligence Community systems engineering and programmatic processes
Experience with spacecraft, payloads, ground systems, launch systems, missile systems, nuclear weapon systems, and/or aircraft systems
A proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with contractors, customers, and corporate staff

jobs.title: Senior Manager or Director, Engineering
jobs.description:
A note on level:

We're evaluating this role at both the Senior Engineering Manager and Director of Engineering level, depending on the candidate's experience and readiness. The scope and core responsibilities described below are the same either way — what differs is title, seniority expectations, and compensation, which will be discussed directly during the interview process. For someone joining as Senior Engineering Manager, there is a path to Director as they grow into the full scope of the role.

About The Role

The growth is proven. Stratus has built a platform customers depend on and a market that is accelerating. The next chapter is scale and compounding value: more customers, deeper workflows, and an AI layer that gives MEP fabrication shops capabilities they could not build on their own.

You will be among the first engineering leaders to put a genuine AI agent into a fabrication workflow that a real shop floor runs on. That has not been done at scale. This role is where it gets built. And you will build it while keeping the core product shipping to a rapidly growing customer base. You will need to hold both.

You will report to the CTO, peer with Directors and Senior Directors across engineering, and partner day to day with the Head of Product and GTM leadership. This role is fully remote. We meet quarterly as a leadership team and make regular visits to customer shop floors. You will know what your software looks like when it is running in a real fabrication environment.

Lead product focused teams delivering against the Stratus roadmap, bringing engineering and AI capability together to ship what customers depend on.

We are early in this build and you will shape how it goes.

This is a lean, senior-IC-adjacent role: the person in this seat is expected to be the anchor — consistently available during core working hours, with occasional availability for production escalations outside business hours (realistically once a month or less, not frequent late nights.)

MEP industry experience is a strong plus.

Success in This Role Looks Like

Customers notice the difference: core platform improvements and AI capabilities that address real workflow problems, solutions that fabrication shops come back for and build their operations around.
AI shipped to production that sticks. Not a proof of concept. Something a shop floor runs on.
Teams that raise their delivery bar consistently and a team stronger than when you found it.
A seat earned in the architecture conversations that shape the platform because you brought engineering judgment and customer insight in equal measure.

What You Will Own

Engineering delivery. Own what ships. Lead PODs that build solutions customers notice and rely on. Favor working software and live demos over status decks. Set the cadence, clear the path, hold the bar.
Customer empathy and connection. Your customers work on a fabrication shop floor. Getting close to them means product conversations, design reviews grounded in real workflows, and staying present when a production issue reaches a customer. Build genuine understanding of what they are trying to accomplish and let that shape how your teams think and build.
Product solutioning. Work alongside Product and users to translate real workflow problems into solutions that stick. The solutions you build will be used on a shop floor by someone who needs them to work every time. Bring engineering judgment to what gets built: knowing when a targeted feature solves the problem, when a deeper architectural change is what is actually needed, and when the right answer is to simplify rather than add.
Technical architecture partnership. Work with the CTO and engineering leadership on platform decisions across our Azure and MongoDB Atlas stack and the move toward agentic surfaces. Full partner in the decisions and fully accountable for how your teams deliver them.
AI era engineering culture. Every stage of the development cycle, from a design whiteboard to a production deploy, should have AI making the team faster and the output better. You build that culture and you go first.
Engineering standards. Leaves the codebase, the process, and the people in better shape than you found them: CI/CD, code review culture, observability, and incident learning treated as foundations, not afterthoughts.
Cross-functional execution. Partner with Product, Data, and Customer Success to ship what customers depend on. Bring what you learn in the field back into how your teams build.

What You Bring

AI forward and pragmatic engineering. Has led a team shipping AI-enabled product features that customers depend on in production, or has otherwise demonstrated strong, hands-on AI/ML depth and sound judgment about where AI adds real value. Agentic-specific experience is a strong plus but not required. Knows what it takes to keep AI reliable in production, makes the right build versus buy call, and focuses on shipping AI customers trust rather than infrastructure for its own sake.
Technical depth. Cloud native SaaS architecture with Azure experience preferred. Comfortable in C# or .NET. MongoDB or document database experience is a plus. "Hands-on" here means staying close to the work — engaging in design reviews, working through technical roadblocks with engineers, and participating in PRs — not necessarily writing production code day to day.
Experience. 10 or more years in software engineering, ideally including experience building and shipping AI-enabled products, with 5 or more in engineering leadership at a SaaS product company (for Director-level candidates; somewhat less leadership tenure may be appropriate for candidates joining at the Senior Engineering Manager level with a path to Director). Has shipped in an environment where the customer base was growing fast enough that a bad release had real consequences. Has taken on a team, nurtured it to higher impact and done it without losing what was already working. Has hired at least one person who became exceptional and can explain exactly why.
Delivery discipline. Real planning, tracking, and follow-through — knows how to hit dates or surface risk early, rather than discovering a miss after the fact. This is the single biggest gap we're solving for with this hire.
Customer and product orientation. Can sit in a customer conversation, find the real problem beneath the stated request, and carry that signal back to the teams. Thinks first about what outcome the customer needs, then about how to deliver it. Measures success in value shipped, not tasks completed.
Leadership experience, including strong communication skills and ability to work with a distributed team and cross functional teams.
Domain (strong plus). MEP, fabrication, or construction technology experience lets you challenge product and architecture decisions with domain intuition and build customer credibility faster.

Nice to Have

Experience with Autodesk or similar
Exposure to manufacturing, supply chain, or field operations software.
Hands on experience with LangGraph, MCP, or agentic orchestration frameworks.

Benefits

Comprehensive and competitive health benefits plan
Matching 401k contributions
20 days annual PTO
Primarily remote work with occasional annual team onsites.

E-VERIFY STATEMENT

Stratus participates in E-Verify. After you join the team, we'll verify your eligibility to work in the U.S. by submitting information from your Form I-9 to the Social Security Administration and, if needed, the Department of Homeland Security. This process happens post-hire only — we never use E-Verify to pre-screen applicants.

jobs.title: Sr. Director- Software Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
Lilly's Purpose
At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our 35,000 employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We're looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.
Come develop great software solutions to solve exciting problems to help patients!
The Software Product Engineering organization is actively looking for a Software Engineering Manager. Are you determined to deliver the best user-centered solutions? Are you ready to own the technical strategy for one or more domains and shape the next generation of application development at Lilly? If so, please apply.

What You'll Be Doing
As the leader of an engineering team accountable for one or more domains, or bounded contexts, within our Commercial or Clinical portfolio, you will set the multi-year technical direction for those domains and use the best of what modern web technologies and architecture have to offer, to design solutions that transform patient experiences and improve treatment outcomes. These products will meet patients where they are due to your close collaboration with our user-experience, product, business, medical, and regulatory partners. You will define the engineering standards, platform investments, and ways of working that extend beyond your own team, and you will partner with business and technology leaders to translate portfolio strategy into a funded, staffed engineering roadmap that is responsive to both business and patient needs. You will also ready your domains for an agentic future: raising the team's fluency with AI-assisted engineering, designing systems and data so that well-governed APIs, tools, and context are available for agents to act on safely, and making deliberate, evidence-based choices about where AI and agentic capabilities create real value for the business and for patients rather than novelty.

How You'll Succeed:
· As a Software Engineering Manager, you will bring both your leadership and technical depth to set direction for the applications and platform capabilities across your domains that exceed product goals and transform the ecosystem.
· Leveraging your strong background in software engineering to guide the team's work, resolve the most ambiguous and technically complex problems, and own technology and architecture direction for the products and platforms in your domains, including build-versus-buy, platform consolidation, and technical-debt investment decisions that play out over multiple planning cycles.
· Owning a multi-year technical roadmap for your domains: sequencing platform investment against business outcomes, quantifying the trade-offs, and defending that plan in annual planning and funding cycles.
· By maximizing the potential of your team, providing guidance, mentorship and growth opportunities, deepening the technical capability of the team, and deliberately developing the next generation of technical leads and people managers, while fostering a collaborative work environment that promotes innovation.
· Matching unique product needs to the resources and skills within your team, while owning headcount planning, budget, and vendor and partner sourcing for your domains, and forecasting capacity several quarters ahead against a demand pipeline you help shape.
· Driving process change beyond your own team, continuously evaluating and enhancing software engineering processes, methodologies, and tools to improve efficiency, quality, and productivity, and establishing the engineering standards and metrics that peer teams adopt.
· Owning the operational health of your domains — service levels, reliability, incident response, security posture, and adherence to data privacy and regulatory requirements — and making the investment case when that health needs attention.
· As a superb communicator and influencer with strong interpersonal skills, you will work and collaborate effectively with your team and product stakeholders, and build alignment across engineering, product, design, and business leadership, representing engineering at the Director and Executive Director level.
· Setting clear objectives, scope and schedules, ensuring the team understands of expectations and priorities, and making transparent, well-reasoned trade-offs when strategy, capacity, and timelines conflict.
· Owning the hiring bar and talent strategy for your domains: attracting strong technical talent, building succession depth for critical roles, and managing performance with candor.

Your Basic Qualifications:
· Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related technical engineering discipline, including Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Information Science, Network Engineering, Systems Engineering, Computer Information Systems (CIS), Management Information Systems (MIS), Cloud Computing, Data Science
· 8+ years working in software engineering roles
· 5+years of experience as a software engineering manager
· Demonstrated experience owning technical strategy and delivery roadmaps for one or more domains, driving execution and outcomes across multiple planning cycles.
· Experience with web and cloud technologies

What You Should Bring:
· Master's degree preferred
· Experience leading multiple concurrent, complex engineering programs from inception to production, including modernizing or retiring legacy systems along the way.
· Deep professional work experience in software engineering, building customer facing applications using Node.js, Vue.js, Python, Java, Scala, Go or Rust.
· Depth across full-stack and platform engineering — RESTful APIs, microservice and event-driven architectures, distributed data management, observability, DevOps and CI/CD, and public cloud (AWS or Azure) — with the judgment to choose among these for a given problem and own the consequences of that choice over the life of the system.
· A strong ability to architect and design robust, high-scale systems and to challenge engineers to think bigger and more generically in developing their solutions, and to make and document durable architectural decisions that other teams build on.
· Demonstrated ability to scope, schedule and resource multiple complex programs in collaboration with cross functional partners and external delivery partners.
· Demonstrated ability to translate business or portfolio strategy into an engineering roadmap, and to communicate that roadmap credibly to senior leadership.
· Self-motivated, independent, and proactive, with outstanding communication skills. Can effectively communicate complex ideas and make compelling arguments, and influence outcomes without formal authority.
· Excellent cross-functional influencer with experience working in a fast-paced environment with frequent context switching, including sustained engagement with senior stakeholders.
· A working understanding of core concepts related to Machine Learning/AI and Data Engineering, and a clear point of view on where they create leverage in your domains.
· Distributed data storage and processing framework experience (Spark and Hadoop).
· Experience growing and maturing software engineering teams and technical leaders, including coaching tech leads and emerging managers, to efficiently deliver high quality software products.
· Experience operating in a regulated environment (healthcare, life sciences, or financial services), with working knowledge of data privacy, security, and quality or compliance expectations for sensitive personal data.

About the Organization
Lilly IT builds and maintains capabilities using groundbreaking technologies like most prominent tech companies. What differentiates Lilly IT is that we create new possibilities through tech to advance our purpose – creating medicines that make life better for people around the world, like data driven drug discovery and connected clinical trials. We hire the best technology professionals from a variety of backgrounds, so they can bring an assortment of knowledge, skills, and diverse thinking to deliver innovative solutions in every area of our business.
Lilly's Software Product Engineering (SPE) organization is focused on building core foundational software platforms to accelerate our ability to reach and support patients digitally. This organization is powered by software engineering experts that solve challenging problems around patient engagement and drug discovery with code.

jobs.description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The Senior Manager, AI/ML Engineering will lead a multidisciplinary team of data scientists, AI/ML engineers, data engineers, and developers to design and deploy enterprise-scale optimization and decision-intelligence solutions that drive measurable business outcomes. This role combines strategic vision with hands-on technical leadership, serving as an enterprise subject matter expert for machine learning, optimization and mathematical programming while guiding teams to deliver production-ready systems that enhance business performance and guest experiences. Key responsibilities include managing a portfolio of applied AI/ML initiatives across personalization, marketing, dynamic pricing, revenue management, workforce planning, digital experiences, and other complex decision domains; translating strategy into execution; embedding responsible AI and decision-system practices; and fostering a culture of innovation. The ideal candidate will be a collaborative leader, committed to developing talent, championing technical rigor, and enabling AI,ML and optimization at scale across the organization.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

Strategic Leadership & Enterprise Enablement

Provide strategic and technical leadership to multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, AI/ML engineers, data engineers, and developers, setting direction and aligning work to enterprise priorities while promoting collaboration, continuous learning, and high-impact delivery.
Establish and communicate a clear enterprise vision, technical roadmap, and operating model for optimization and decision intelligence, balancing immediate business needs with long-term capability development.
Direct technical teams by defining objectives, decision rights, technical standards, architectural guardrails, and measurable outcomes.
Guide and mentor technical teams through problem formulation, architecture, model design, solution trade-offs, and production readiness in support of machine learning, optimization and mathematical programming.
Coordinate initiative sequencing, resource needs, dependencies, and delivery risks across product, engineering, data, and business teams, removing roadblocks and ensuring execution remains aligned with scope, schedule, and business outcomes.

Applied AI/ML & Optimization Development

Provide technical direction and oversight for AI/ML and optimization development, architecture, code quality, reusable libraries, reference architectures, and product-lifecycle best practices to ensure scalable, maintainable, secure, and production-ready solutions.
Engage with internal and external partners to gather requirements and collaborate with engineers, architects, product leaders, and business stakeholders to design robust solutions across domains.
Lead end-to-end problem formulation, model design, algorithm selection, prototyping, benchmarking, and validation across optimization, machine learning, and decision science. Apply advanced analytical and AI/ML techniques to integrate predictive and prescriptive modeling, experimentation, simulation, real-time signals, and business constraints into scalable decision systems that improve business outcomes and adapt over time.
Establish delivery and operational governance, remove cross-team roadblocks, and track quality, reliability, adoption, and business-impact KPIs. Define standards for model and solver monitoring, performance degradation and drift detection, incident response, and continuous improvement.

AI/ML Technical Strategy

Define and drive the strategy and prioritized portfolio for optimization products and decision systems, balancing near-term business outcomes with long-term platform evolution and determining where capabilities should be built, bought, reused, or standardized across personalization, marketing, dynamic pricing, revenue management, workforce planning, digital experiences, and resource allocation.
Evaluate open-source and commercial solvers, frameworks, and platforms across performance, cost, scalability, licensing, and security; direct cross-functional alignment on technology choices, investments, standards, and responsible-AI requirements, and communicate recommendations, trade-offs, and program status to senior leadership.
Understands and actively participates in Environmental, Health & Safety responsibilities by following established UO policy, procedures, training and team member involvement activities.
Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Hands-on experience designing and developing production decision systems, including data and feature pipelines, APIs and services, cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure, version control, automated testing, CI/CD, containerization, observability, model monitoring, drift detection, and retraining or recalibration processes.
Deep expertise in statistical inference, supervised and unsupervised learning, regression, classification, clustering and segmentation, time-series forecasting, probabilistic modeling, predictive analytics, and model ensembling.
Demonstrated expertise formulating and solving large-scale decision problems using linear, mixed-integer, nonlinear, stochastic, robust, and/or multi-objective optimization; experience with constraint programming, decomposition, simulation, heuristics, and learning-based decision methods.
Advanced proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience using optimization modeling frameworks and one or more solver ecosystems such as Gurobi or CPLEX.
Experience integrating optimization with machine learning, forecasting, predictive models, personalization and recommendation systems, experimentation, simulation, or adaptive decision methods.
Proven ability to establish technical vision, influence and direct multidisciplinary teams without formal authority, drive cross-functional alignment, and resolve complex technical and business decisions.
Track record of connecting technical solutions to tangible business value and managing a portfolio of initiatives across multiple business domains.
Storyteller comfortable presenting to executives and mentoring both technical and non-technical audiences.
Hands-on experience applying privacy, security, fairness, explainability, governance, and compliance principles in production AI/ML and optimization systems.
Advanced knowledge of product and delivery methodologies, with demonstrated success translating strategy into coordinated execution in fast-paced, ambiguous, and matrixed environments.

EDUCATION:

Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science or in a relevant applied quantitative field is required.

EXPERIENCE:

9+ years’ experience in applied‑AI, data science or software‑engineering roles;
or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Your talent, skills and experience will be rewarded with a competitive compensation package.

Utilize CAD and SolidWorks to create, develop and refine product designs.

Senior Engineering Manager – Checkfront & Regiondo

About The Role

We’re looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the teams responsible for Checkfront and Regiondo, established booking-management products used by thousands of tour, activity, and experience operators.

Checkfront and Regiondo are mature, revenue-generating products with years of functionality and customer needs represented in their codebases. The teams will continue delivering meaningful product improvements while placing increased emphasis on stability, reliability, performance, maintainability, and operational confidence.

As a Senior Engineering Manager, you will be accountable for the health, development, performance, and delivery of the engineering teams for both products. You’ll work closely with Product, senior technical contributors and other engineering leaders to establish priorities, make sound tradeoffs, and create an environment in which engineers can effectively work and grow.

We employ a player-coach model for engineering leadership. You won’t be expected to be the team’s primary implementer or sole technical decision maker, and your success will not be measured by your personal output. You will, however, be expected to remain close enough to the work to represent the major systems, architectural decisions, delivery risks, incidents, and operational characteristics across your area. You should be able to explain the technical approach for both teams, participate credibly in engineering discussions, and make high-level decisions.

This is a role for a technical leader who enjoys leading people as well as improving how engineering teams build and deliver quality software.

What You’ll Do

Lead and Develop Teams

Set clear expectations and create an environment of trust, accountability, and respectful collaboration across the Checkfront and Regiondo teams
Hold effective one-on-ones and provide timely, specific, actionable feedback
Support engineers in building meaningful growth plans and developing their careers
Recognize strong performance and address performance concerns directly
Develop senior engineers and emerging technical leaders, creating opportunities for them to take on broader responsibilities
Maintain awareness of team morale, workload, delivery constraints, interpersonal dynamics, and capacity
Participate in hiring and onboarding new team members as the teams evolve

Own Multi-Team Delivery and Operational Outcomes

Partner closely with Product to establish priorities, sequencing, and delivery plans across both products, aligning to the tech organization’s overall goals
Create alignment when teams have shared dependencies, competing priorities, or overlapping ownership
Balance new product development with reliability, maintenance, testing, technical debt, performance, and longer-term engineering health
Surface delivery risks, dependencies, ownership gaps and capacity constraints early
Establish clear ownership and hold teams accountable for delivering work to an appropriate quality standard
Remain actively engaged in production incidents and escalations, understanding their customer impact, contributing factors, and remediation
Maintain accountability for stable, secure deployments and appropriate post-deployment observability

Provide Technical and Operational Leadership

Maintain sufficient technical and operational context across Checkfront and Regiondo to understand their major systems, dependencies, risks, and incidents
Identify opportunities to make team processes and engineering practices more effective
Participate in important technical discussions, challenge assumptions, and help the team make pragmatic tradeoffs
Help the teams improve maintainability, observability, testing, reliability, and overall engineering quality
Ensure that technical investments are connected to meaningful customer, product, operational, or business outcomes
Stay hands-on enough with both team’s work and systems to understand the practical constraints the engineers are working within
Use evidence to understand whether changes to tools or working practices are actually improving team outcomes

What We’re Looking For

Experience successfully leading and developing software engineers in an Engineering Manager, Senior Engineering Manager, or comparable engineering leadership role
Experience operating across multiple engineering teams and product areas
Strong people-management skills, including coaching, feedback, career development, expectation setting, and addressing performance concerns
Experience developing senior engineers or technical leaders
A track record of creating accountability without relying on micromanagement
Strong operational instincts, including experience with production incidents, observability, reliability, and learning from recurring failures
Strong written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to communicate engineering concerns to Product, Support, leadership, and other stakeholders
An ownership mindset: when something affecting your area is going wrong, you stay engaged until there is clarity around impact, ownership, next steps, and resolution

Nice to Have

Familiarity with some of the technologies used across Checkfront and Regiondo, including PHP, React, PostgreSQL, and Google Cloud Platform
Experience working closely with customer-facing teams such as Support or Customer Success
Experience with AI-assisted software-development tools and an interest in applying them pragmatically and responsibly
Experience in booking, ecommerce, travel, tours and activities, or other operationally complex domains
Experience helping teams incrementally modernize complex systems without requiring large-scale rewrites
Experience improving test coverage, deployment automation, incident response, and production observability

Join Our Team

In 2025, USA Today recognized Primerica as a Top Workplace USA for the fifth year in a row, and Newsweek named Primerica one of America’s Greatest Workplaces for Diversity for the second consecutive year. In 2024, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution named Primerica as a Top Workplace for the eleventh consecutive year, and Forbes recognized Primerica as one of America’s Best Employers for Women for the fifth year in a row. In addition, for the tenth time Primerica has been voted a Best Employer by Gwinnett Magazine. Primerica is a great place to work! Join our team to experience what it’s like to work at “one of the best places to work in the metro Atlanta”.

About This Position

Primerica is seeking an experienced and technical Vice President of Infrastructure & Operations to lead the strategy, engineering, delivery, and ongoing operation of the company's infrastructure platforms and technology services. This role is responsible for enterprise hosting, cloud services, storage, networking, telecommunications, end-user computing, messaging and collaboration platforms, workplace technology services, disaster recovery, and infrastructure operations. The Vice President will ensure technology services are secure, resilient, scalable, and cost-effective while supporting business growth, operational excellence, and technology modernization initiatives.

This position is based at Primerica's Duluth, Georgia headquarters and follows a hybrid work model, with an expectation of onsite presence approximately 2-3 days per week. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship.

The salary range for this role is $195,000 - $230,000.

Responsibilities & Qualifications

Develop and execute an enterprise infrastructure and operations strategy aligned with business objectives, technology modernization efforts, and long-term architectural direction.
Lead the design, delivery, and operation of highly available infrastructure services, including compute, storage, virtualization, cloud, network, and telecommunications platforms.
Oversee end-user computing and workplace technology services, including endpoint management, desktop engineering, mobility, service desk, and employee productivity solutions.
Direct enterprise messaging, collaboration, and communication platforms, ensuring secure, reliable, and highly available services for employees and field representatives.
Lead 24x7 infrastructure operations, including service delivery, incident management, problem management, monitoring, operational readiness, and continuous service improvement.
Drive automation, operational efficiency, and service management maturity through ITSM best practices and process optimization.
Establish infrastructure capacity planning, performance management, and technology lifecycle strategies to ensure scalability, reliability, and operational resilience.
Partner with Information Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to ensure infrastructure platforms meet security, regulatory, and resiliency requirements.
Lead disaster recovery and business continuity planning, testing, and execution to minimize operational risk and downtime.
Manage infrastructure financial planning, budgets, vendor relationships, contract negotiations, and strategic technology partnerships.
Build and develop high-performing technology teams while fostering accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Collaborate with business and technology leaders to identify infrastructure needs and deliver technology solutions that improve productivity, efficiency, and customer outcomes.

Essential Skills & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or equivalent industry experience.
10+ years of progressive infrastructure leadership experience, including 5+ years in a senior leadership role.
Deep experience leading enterprise infrastructure organizations across hosting, cloud, networking, telecommunications, end-user computing, messaging, collaboration, workplace technology, and disaster recovery disciplines.
Expertise in enterprise infrastructure technologies including Windows and Linux platforms, IBM Power Systems, virtualization technologies, x86 server environments, cloud platforms (AWS and Azure), enterprise storage, networking, identity services, messaging systems, and collaboration platforms.
Strong understanding of ITIL/ITSM service management practices, operational governance, infrastructure security controls, and regulatory compliance requirements.
Experience leading large-scale infrastructure and operations teams supporting mission-critical business environments with high availability and service level commitments.
